_meta.name: CareLoop Master Canonical Parameter Dictionary
_meta.changelog: v1.1.0: cross-checked v1.0.0 ranges against web sources (Mayo Clinic, Cleveland Clinic, MedlinePlus, LabCorp/Quest-cited ranges, StatPearls, NCEP ATP III/AHA lipid guidance, Geeky Medics clinical reference tables, ACP reference-range tables) rather than training data alone; corrected HDL to open_lower_bound (higher is protective, not a fixed band), adjusted ALP and total bilirubin to better-corroborated ranges, and added 10 parameters (amylase, lipase, D-dimer, ANA, anti-TPO, LH, FSH, beta-hCG, BNP, ammonia) identified during research as common in comprehensive panels but missing from v1.0.0.
_meta.known_limitation: Reference ranges here are unisex adult defaults. Cross-checking confirmed several parameters have clinically meaningful sex-specific (hemoglobin, hematocrit, RBC, ferritin, uric acid, testosterone, estradiol, ALT/AST, GGT) and some age/life-stage-specific (pregnancy thyroid panel, pediatric CBC) reference ranges that this version does not yet model separately — flagged as the next dictionary enhancement rather than silently assumed away.
_meta.important_note: typical_reference_range is a FALLBACK default only. Whenever a source lab report prints its own reference range for a result, that printed range must be stored alongside the value and used for in-range/out-of-range flagging for that result — the dictionary default is used only when a report omits a range, and for cross-report plausibility validation (see PRD Section 4.6). This matters more than usual here: verified sources for the same parameter (e.g. WBC, ALT, ALP) disagreed with each other by meaningful margins, confirming there is no single universal ground truth range to encode.
